claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free prep area, cookware, or boiling water is mentioned anywhere in available sources.

The house broth is a mackerel-and-bonito dashi typical of soba tsuyu, which in Japan is almost always seasoned with standard wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce or tamari option was mentioned.

The core menu (meat soba, mackerel-bonito dashi broth, offal dishes at dinner) is built around fish and meat stock, so vegan diners cannot rely on shared broth or sauces being incidentally plant-based.
The soba flour is a coarse whole-grain (hikigurumi) buckwheat, and one visiting blogger judged the noodles close to juuwari (100% buckwheat) with a fragrant, hearty texture.

name: 南インド料理 シリバラジ 水道橋店 (Sri Balaji Suidobashi)

claims.text: All lunch meal sets (Regular Meals ¥890, Chennai Meals ¥990, Sri Balaji Special Meals ¥1,200) come with 'ライス or ナン' (rice OR naan) plus papad — directly contradicting the GF label's claim that no naan/roti was found.
The Special Thali set includes 'プーリ or チャパティ' (poori OR chapati) alongside chicken/mutton/fish curry, rasam, chicken 65, papad, basmati rice, salad, curd, dessert — multiple wheat breads on the menu.
120-minute all-you-can-eat + all-you-can-drink banquet plan, ¥4,500, ~68 dishes including pakoda — buffet service with shared serving utensils is a major cross-contamination vector for celiac diners.

Reservation/allergy handling amounts only to a generic note: 'If you have allergies, please consult with us.' No gluten-free labeling, dedicated prep, or cross-contamination protocol is described anywhere.
南インドのベジタリアンメニュー代表のサンバルをはじめ、豆のペーストを揚げたワダなどヘルシーでユニークな料理がたくさんあります。また、米と魚のカレーや新鮮な野菜を使用したベジタリアンのメニューもお任せくださいとのことです。

name: スケロク ダイナー (SUKE6 DINER (Sukeroku Diner))

claims.text: The diner operates its own on-site bakery ("Manufacture") baking fresh bread daily, meaning wheat flour is present and handled throughout the kitchen; no source confirms separated gluten-free prep.
Search of GF/celiac review channels surfaced no celiac corroboration of GF handling; the only GF artifact is a single 'Gluten-Free Omelets' photo on FindMeGlutenFree with no protocol described.

Venue described as serving 'natural yeast bread baked in the workshop on the third floor' (croissants, bagels, pain au chocolat) — confirms an on-site flour/wheat-saturated bakery integral to the kitchen, undermining any default GF-safe claim.

Described as 'a brunch and dinner place serving western food with few vegetarian and vegan options' — vegan is limited, not a core offering, consistent with 'options' ceiling and no vegan-dedicated handling.
Concept centers on in-house charcuterie, eggs, and bread ('EAT GOOD', additive-free charcuterie, farm eggs) — a wheat-, egg-, and meat-forward menu with no stated allergen/celiac protocol.
Described as a Western-food diner and bakery with only a few vegetarian and vegan menu items, rather than a vegan-focused kitchen.
Guidance for visitors is to tell staff about vegetarian/vegan preferences and any allergies before choosing a menu item, rather than relying on menu marks alone.

Menu carries English translations and vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free tags on select items (e.g., a gluten-free buddha bowl, a soy/green-tea latte), and the kitchen avoids chemical seasonings, making ingredients more transparent than a typical diner.
All charcuterie, dressings, and drinks (bacon, ginger ale, lemonade, etc.) are handmade in-house from named ingredient sources rather than bought pre-made, reducing hidden additive risk.

name: 大勝軒まるいち 渋谷店 (Taishoken Maruichi Shibuya)

claims.text: Noodles are handmade from wheat flour, water, egg, and kansui (lye water) — this is a traditional wheat-based tsukemen shop with no gluten-free noodle alternative mentioned anywhere.

The dipping broth is simmered from pork bone, chicken carcass, vegetables, and dried fish, and standard bowls come topped with pork chashu and a soft-boiled egg — there is no vegan broth or protein option described.

name: 大衆居酒屋 とりいちず 水道橋店 (Taishū Izakaya Toriichizu Suidōbashi-ten)

claims.text: Karaage and other fried items are coated in a wheat-flour-based spiced breading and cooked in a shared kitchen fryer used for multiple menu items; no dedicated gluten-free fryer or process is advertised.
The restaurant's bone-in chicken and grilled skewers are finished with a proprietary tare (sauce); tare at Japanese izakayas is soy-sauce based and contains wheat.
The signature mizutaki hot pot broth is slow-simmered from chicken bones for 8+ hours; no vegetable or plant-based broth alternative is listed.

name: タムジャイサムゴー 新宿中央通り店（譚仔三哥） (TamJai SamGor Shinjuku Chuo-dori)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free kitchen/fryer is confirmed; the menu includes wheat-containing items (e.g. pork wontons) made in the same kitchen as the rice-noodle soups.

FindMeGlutenFree listing for TamJai SamGor (Shinjuku City): staff advised that noodles are made with wheat so no dishes are ok, and the chicken and other meat has sauces that are not suitable for gluten-free diets; establishment is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility and may not be safe for those with celiac disease.

Documented TamJai SamGor soup base is water + pork-bone (or chicken) broth + chicken powder + evaporated milk + peppercorn oil + chili — none confirmed wheat-free, and contains dairy; not a vegan/GF-safe base.

Japanese gluten-free guidance surfaced in search: TamJai uses gluten-free rice noodles but 'most menu items contain wheat components,' and soy sauce/seasonings typically contain wheat, so wheat-allergic diners must confirm with staff — no celiac protocol documented.

Brand/delivery 'gluten-free' labeling (Uber Eats store names, brand site) applies to the mixian ingredient only; no dedicated fryer, allergen certification, or wheat-free tare/broth is claimed for celiac handling.

Vegetarian mushroom base and vegetarian toppings are described for the international/HK menu, not confirmed for the Japan/Shinjuku branch, whose menu leans pork wontons, clams, fish balls and chicken wings.

Menu toppings include pork wontons, clams, and (per delivery listings) fish balls and fried chicken wings, indicating soup bases and shared prep are not run as a vegan kitchen even when a vegetable-topped noodle bowl is ordered.
The signature 米線 (mixian) rice noodles are made from just rice and water, so they are naturally gluten-free — this is called out directly in the store's own delivery-platform listing title.
A vegetable-forward option exists: diners can reduce the noodle portion or substitute lettuce for noodles, topped with a variety of fresh vegetables.

The core tempura batter across the menu is a wheat-flour, cornstarch, rice-flour and beer mixture leavened with dry yeast and tinted with tomato powder — there is no separate gluten-free batter or fryer described.

The signature and most-discussed dishes are seafood-based, using shrimp mousseline blended with Vietnamese fish sauce (nyokumamu) and finished with an Américaine sauce made from shrimp heads and shells — animal products run through the core preparation, not just as a garnish.

name: 手打そば大庵 (Teuchi Soba Daian)

claims.text: Noodles are made with a stone-milled buckwheat dough that includes roughly 20% wheat flour as a binder, so all standard soba served here contains gluten — there is no all-buckwheat (juwari) or gluten-free noodle option identified.
As a traditional soba specialty shop, the tsuyu dipping sauce follows standard shoyu-based preparation; no wheat-free soy sauce or gluten-free tsuyu alternative was mentioned in any source found.
Menu includes duck confit and charcoal-grilled chicken, and traditional soba tsuyu is typically made with katsuobushi (bonito) dashi; no vegan menu, plant-based dashi, or vegan labeling was found.
